correctness.rationale: Uses the complete harmonic-wavelet basis of De Mari–Monti–Rizzo Theorem 14 for q>=2 alpha>1. Distinct wavelets cancel separately on each horocycle: disjoint cones trivial, same root orthogonal child zero-sum vectors, nested roots ancestral wavelet constant on descendants of lower root at each height while child-zero-sum wavelet totals zero. Descendants at level h(v)+m have total squared wavelet amplitude q^(m-1)[(1-s^m)/(1-s)]²; with weight q^(-alpha h), the normalized eigenvalue on root height k is lambda(k)=W(1)^(-1)sum_{m>=1} r^m(1-s^m)² phi(k+m), r=q^(1-alpha),s=1/q. Rational W(z)=r(1-s)² z(1+rsz)/[(1-rz)(1-rsz)(1-rs²z)] follows by three geometric series; shift S is invertible on l∞(Z) and all four factor inverses converge for r<1. Q(-z)=(1+rz)(1+rsz)(1+rs²z)/(1-rsz) has strictly positive Taylor coefficients, giving exact inverse l∞ norm kappa=(1+r)(1+rs)²(1+rs²)/[(1-r)(1-rs)²(1-rs²)], attained by alternating sequences; constants attain norm upper bound. Each horocycle has infinitely many roots, so every labeled eigenvalue has infinite multiplicity and sigma=sigma_ess=closure of its range; surjectivity gives block-constant diagonal C* algebra, no nonzero compact. Independently computed exact benchmark q=2,alpha=2: W(1)=10/21, W(-1)=-2/45, kappa=75/7. Infinite-dimensional completeness comes from the cited primary theorem, not finite-depth checks.
